correctness.rationale: For each n>=7 the cubic graph GP(n,3) has a perfect-matching cut iff a binary shore coloring has exactly one opposite-color neighbor at each vertex. Its outer bits a_i determine b_i uniquely by the 3-bit local rule; forbidden isolated outer bits have no extension. The inner condition is a check on nine outer bits, hence a length-n closed walk in the 8-bit de Bruijn overlap digraph. I reconstructed all 512 candidate nine-bit tests and confirmed precisely 90 arcs. Repeated in/out pruning retains exactly 42,20,16 states, with the final induced graph consisting solely of loops (0),(255), a 4-cycle (51,153,204,102), and two 5-cycles (24,140,198,99,49), (57,156,206,231,115). Each closed walk is a labeled cyclic outer coloring for any n, even when the nine-bit window wraps repeatedly; the inner bits are unique. Thus 2+4[4|n]+10[5|n] colorings, quotient by fixed-point-free global complement gives 1+2[4|n]+5[5|n] cuts. Direct independent enumeration of 2^(n-1) normalized outer colorings for n=7..11 returned counts (1,3,1,6,1) and exact crossing-spoke strata (n), (n and 0), (n), (n and n/5), (n). Finite samples corroborate, whereas the exhaustive state certificate and closed-walk bijection prove the universal claim.
residual_risks: The classification concerns crossing-edge perfect matchings only, not all perfect matchings whose deletion disconnects graph; k=3, n>=7, simple graph.
